newsitem.title: UK: Labour unreliable on schools, health - UK's Ashdown.
newsitem.headline: Labour unreliable on schools, health - UK's Ashdown.

text.p: The Labour Party has now made it clear that it cannot be relied on to improve the state of education in Britain, or the National Health Service, Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown said on Wednesday.

His sharp attack on the official opposition was prompted by the speech this week of Labour's economics spokesman Gordon Brown, who said Labour would not raise either the standard or the top rates of income tax in the next parliament.

"After Gordon Brown's speech on Monday, it is now crystal clear that if you are concerned about the state of our schools or the NHS, the Liberal Democrats are the only party that will make a difference," Ashdown told his parliamentary candidates gathered in London.

The Liberal Democrats have proposed a 50 percent top rate of income tax for people earning more than 100,000 pounds a year, and pledged to increase the standard rate by one percentage point if the money is needed to improve education.
"(Teachers) know they have been let down by this government, but now they know they cannot rely on Labour to make things any better," Ashdown said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
